queries.text: Under any gauge-invariant probability measure on lattice link variables, the small-field event that every link lies near the identity has probability exponentially small in the number of sites for every value of the coupling; the exponent is supplied by the links of a maximal tree, which are independent and Haar-distributed

Why gauge invariance alone forces the all-links-near-identity small-field set to have exponentially small measure in the lattice volume regardless of beta: maximal-tree (axial) gauge fixing shows the tree links are i.i.d. uniform under Haar measure, which gives the exponential bound

Gauge-orbit obstruction to concentration near the trivial holonomy configuration: a law invariant under local gauge transformations cannot make the small-field chart likely; its probability decays exponentially in the volume at every coupling, with the rate set by an independent family of Haar-uniform links (the maximal tree)

Large-field probability lower bound from gauge invariance: exponential-in-volume suppression of the event that all link variables stay close to the identity, uniform in the coupling, derived from the mutually independent uniformly distributed links of a spanning tree gauge
